claims.text: Increasing FCC/BCC interphase-boundary density enhances the creep resistance of the dual-phase HEA coating.
FCC/BCC interphase boundaries impede dislocation motion.
Increasing interphase-boundary density promotes more uniform strain partitioning during continuous loading.
The as-deposited coating has FCC dendrites containing embedded BCC or B2 precipitates.
This FCC-dendrite/BCC-or-B2-precipitate morphology is typical of the protective coating.
Deposition or heat-treatment changes can systematically vary interphase-boundary density while overall composition remains constant.
Sustained elevated-temperature continuous loading represents the relevant creep-testing condition.
Interphase-boundary density and distribution are the proposed structural mediators of creep resistance.
A higher interphase-boundary density produces more dislocation pile-ups.
FCC/BCC phase contrast and interfaces redistribute local strain between phases.
Dislocation obstruction and strain redistribution delay progressive creep deformation.
At otherwise identical creep conditions, specimens with higher interphase-boundary density will have a lower creep rate than the standard-boundary-density baseline.
At otherwise identical creep conditions, specimens with higher interphase-boundary density will undergo less progressive plastic deformation than the baseline.
The proposed effect is expected only while the dual-phase microstructure remains stable under sustained elevated-temperature stress.
Phase volume fraction and defect distributions may independently influence deformation and the measured creep rate.

Failure to observe a statistically significant creep-rate decrease or delayed progressive deformation in the higher-boundary-density specimens would falsify the proposed boundary-density control of creep resistance.

contradictions.description: The intervention proposes altering deposition or heat-treatment parameters to change boundary density, whereas the falsification design says the compared specimens will maintain the same processing history. Boundary density cannot be varied through those processing changes while processing history is also held constant.
